messages:
Alex Chong: Hey — seeing a weird flake in the Android sample app using our Kotlin SDK. Intermittent socket close during auth refresh, and okhttp seems to suppress retries so user-visible error.
Maya Patel: ugh. which okhttp version? stacktrace or logs?
Alex Chong: okhttp 4.11.0. Logs show connection closed right after request body start, then our interceptor gets a 401, triggers token refresh, retry is attempted but okhttp returns java.net.SocketException: SSL handshake aborted: read 
Alex Chong: log snippets:
```
D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
D/OkHttp: Content-Length: 1024
W/Net: Connection closed by peer during body write
E/MySdk: Request failed: java.net.SocketException: Socket closed
I/AuthRefresh: refreshing token (background)
I/AuthRefresh: token refresh success
D/OkHttp: retrying request with new token
E/OkHttp: Suppressing retry due to prior connection failure (early EOF)
```
Samir Rao: is the suppressed retry coming from our RetryInterceptor or okhttp's internal policy?
Maya Patel: looks like okhttp is avoiding the retry because the stream was half-consumed? If body was streamed, it can't be replayed unless it's repeatable. Are you using RequestBody that can be rewritten?
Alex Chong: sample app uses streaming RequestBody for large prompts (we tried to avoid buffering). The behavior changed vs earlier tests: before, our RetryInterceptor would buffer small bodies and replay; now it just bails.
Alex Chong: config: Retrofit + OkHttp client with an AuthInterceptor that blocks and refreshes token synchronously, then a RetryInterceptor that retries once after refresh.
Maya Patel: two things to check: 1) enable call.clone() path for retries? 2) make RequestBody repeatable (e.g., ByteArray or use Buffer) for retries. Also check connection pool / keepalive on Android 14 emulator — there are reports of early FINs.
Samir Rao: another angle: when refresh happens on the same thread, the original call might have closed the stream. We should ensure the retry happens on a fresh Call object: call.clone().execute(). Our RetryInterceptor should wrap and re-create the request, not reuse the old stream.
Alex Chong: good point. current retry code does: chain.proceed(request) after refresh, expecting okhttp to handle it. If body is one-shot, that's doomed.
Maya Patel: can you paste the RetryInterceptor snippet?
Alex Chong: small snippet:
```
class RetryInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val request = chain.request()
    val response = chain.proceed(request)
    if (response.code == 401) {
      AuthManager.refreshIfNeeded()
      val newReq = request.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${AuthManager.token}")
        .build()
      return chain.proceed(newReq)
    }
    return response
  }
}
```
Samir Rao: yeah that's the issue — chain.proceed(request) consumes the body stream. For a retry you need to create a fresh Call (call.clone()) or ensure RequestBody is replayable. Interceptor chain doesn't automatically rewind non-repeatable bodies.
Maya Patel: practical fix: for sample app, change to BufferingRequestBody for streams smaller than X, or add logic to fail-fast and surface a nicer error informing user to use buffered body for retries.
Alex Chong: ok. Quick test: I'll switch sample to ByteArrayRequestBody for <=64KB and see if retry becomes reliable.
deploy-bot: FYI: created issue RD-INF-7482 for "android sdk: intermittent socket close + non-replayable body causes suppressed retry" and linked sample app repro.
Alex Chong: thanks — repro steps sent in the issue. Also adding a note in onboarding docs: streaming bodies may not be replayable across auth refresh.
Maya Patel: nice. long-term we should make SDK RetryInterceptor smarter: detect non-repeatable body and either buffer transparently up to limit or return a helpful error telling devs to buffer.
Samir Rao: agree. Also add unit test with MockWebServer that closes connection mid-body to ensure we don't regress.
Alex Chong: will do. Patch incoming to sample app and a docs blurb. :thumbsup:
